correctness.rationale: PASS: Reconstructed the Harris--Tu degree product D_(n,n-c)=prod_(j=0..c-1) [binom(n+j,c)/binom(c+j,c)] for 1<=c<=n-1, and rectangular Schur/Jacobi--Trudi determinant det[binom(n,c-i+j)]_(1<=i,j<=c). If n=p^e, Lucas says binom(n,k)=0 mod p for all 1<=k<=n-1; the determinant has every entry on/below diagonal divisible by p, so det=0 mod p. Also D_(n,n-1)=n, so no other prime can divide all degrees. Conversely when p|n and n/p^e>1, choose c=p^e<n. In F_p, Lucas yields binom(n+j,c) ≡n/p^e (mod p) for 0<=j<c, and binom(c+j,c) ≡1 (mod p); every factor is a p-adic unit, hence the particular degree is nonzero mod p. Thus no p divides all degrees; primes outside n excluded by D_(n,n-1)=n. Rational independent recalculation of all coranks n=2..25 recovered the gcd dichotomy and explicit escaping coranks. The finite data only corroborate the Lucas/determinant universal argument.

value.rationale: PASS: The gcd across all nested singular-rank loci is a natural arithmetic invariant distinct from any one degree; its sharp prime-power/composite separation, and an explicit rank avoiding each candidate common prime, are motivated complete classifications. The theorem does not pretend that Lucas, Harris--Tu, or the degree product is new, and explicitly leaves exact common exponents unresolved.

final_claim: Let D_(n,r) be the classical projective degree of the generic complex n×n matrix rank-at-most-r determinantal variety for every proper 1<=r<n. Their gcd G_n is 1 unless n is a prime power; when n=p^e its only prime divisor is p (the exact valuation for e>1 is not claimed). For any p|n with n/p^νp(n)>1, the rank stratum of corank p^νp(n) has degree prime to p.
limitations: Product and determinant identities are classical; new component is simultaneous gcd theorem.
No extrapolation from computed n<=25; Lucas proof supplies arbitrary n.
